svg.title: I2C multi-controller bus access policies: timeline S2
svg.text: S2: 3 saturated controllers, m = 0.1 Tmax = 2 ms
50 ms = 2.5 Tmax shown; verdicts and utilisation from the full 2 s run
Tmax = 20 ms, tbuf = 0.78 µs, r = 60 µs (measured), margin = 10 µs, tidle = 10 µs, W = 100 µs
Tmax: 1024 bytes × 9 bit / 800 kbit/s (set 1 Mbit/s) = 11.52 ms + 2.7 ms clock stretching = 14.22 ms, rounded up to 20 ms
Controller A → target 0x10 (lowest address, wins ties)
transmitting (colour = sending controller, label = target address)
packet queued, holding off (re-arm r or policy deferral)
Arbitration is decided by the target address: of the controllers that START together, the one sending to the lowest address wins.
C never gets the bus · A and B alternate
Bus busy → wait for STOP; arbitration lost → retry at once; after its own STOP a controller needs its re-arm time r before it competes again.
every controller gets the bus · worst access delay 20.0 ms = 1.00 Tmax
After its own STOP a controller waits Tmax + margin before it competes again.
every controller gets the bus · worst access delay 4.01 ms = 0.20 Tmax
After its own STOP a controller waits until the bus has been idle for tidle; controllers that have not had their turn compete as soon as the bus is free.
every controller gets the bus · worst access delay 26.2 ms = 1.31 Tmax
Before every attempt a controller probes the bus; bus busy or arbitration lost → back off a random time in (0, W] and probe again; after its own STOP it waits
time [ms]; darker gridlines every Tmax = 20 ms
Every controller always has a packet of length m = 0.1 Tmax = 2 ms queued. Controllers waiting when the bus becomes free start together tbuf after STOP; the lowest
At this scale 1 px = 50 µs: tbuf = 0.78 µs, tidle = 10 µs, r = 60 µs, margin = 10 µs and W = 100 µs are far too small to draw, so adjacent bars that seem to touch are
in fact separated by such gaps.
Policy 1: waiting controllers start tbuf = 0.78 µs after STOP, the previous winner only after r = 60 µs, so it cannot take the next START; but r < m + 2·tbuf, so it is
re-armed before the STOP after that and beats C again: A and B alternate, C starves. Only r < tbuf would let A keep the bus; C would get turns only for r > m + 2·tbuf
Policy 2 holds a controller off for Tmax + margin = 20.01 ms after its own STOP; with 2 ms packets the bus then stays idle: utilisation 27.3 % = N·m / (m + Tmax
Policy 3: after every round the bus is idle for tidle, which re-arms all controllers; worst access delay 4.01 ms = (N − 1)·m + (N − 1)·tbuf + tidle; utilisation
Policy 4: after every STOP the waiting controllers probe at random times and the first probe takes the bus; the last sender first waits r plus a backoff, so it rarely
wins the next transfer. Turns A 333, B 335, C 322 (2 s run): the address no longer decides who sends, but the order is random, so a controller may lose several times
in a row: worst access delay 26.2 ms = 1.31 Tmax (policy 3: 4.01 ms). The bus stays idle until the first probe, on average 20.2 µs per transfer: utilisation 99.0 %;
each controller probes about 13 200 times per second.
